page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 959 GB SSD. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the processor and memory subsystems operate in lower performance tiers. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 10% to 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also show limitations, with large-block read-only operations registering in the bottom 10% at 19.71 GB/sec and write operations in the bottom 25% at 18.31 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, similarly rank in the bottom 10%.

Given the hardware profile, the ecs.i2.xlarge offers a qualitative balance of high local storage capacity and memory density relative to its compute power, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. However, the weak CPU and memory bandwidth performance present a clear tradeoff for compute-heavy applications. It is best suited for memory-intensive or storage-centric workloads with moderate processing demands, such as local database caching, lightweight file serving, or basic data-buffering tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.xlarge is an x86_64 server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 959 GB local SSD. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results place its CPU and memory performance in the lower tiers, with Geekbench and stress-ng scores falling in the bottom 10% to 25%. Large-block memory read bandwidth is limited to 19.71 GB/sec. While compute-heavy tasks are constrained by these performance profiles, the instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core alongside substantial local SSD storage. This combination makes the ecs.i2.xlarge qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-optimized or storage-centric workloads that require moderate processing power, such as database caching, lightweight web serving, and basic data storage operations.
